deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and no handwriting by Riemann. It is p. 387 of a printed journal offprint: F. Beilstein, 'Ueber zwei neue Derivate der salicyligen Säure', Nachrichten der Göttinger Societät, Nr. 5, presented 6 December (late 1850s). The pencil '13' in the margin is the archival foliation (Bl. 13); the printed sheet presumably survived among Riemann's papers as scrap paper or a wrapper. The page is chemistry, so what can be reconstructed is the chemistry.

(1) Starting idea, from the previous page. Aldehyde-ammonia treated with HCN and HCl gives alanine (the Strecker reaction), and valeraldehyde-ammonia gives leucine. Beilstein expects the 'hydramides' of aromatic aldehydes to behave the same way. The experiments were carried out by A. Reinecke.

(2) Hydrosalicylamide (Spirimid) is (C7H5(OH)CH=)3N2. It forms as 3 C7H6O2 + 2 NH3 - 3 H2O = C21H18N2O3 (this derivation is mine; the formula itself is the one given on the page). The formulas use the new atomic weights C=12, O=16, marked in the print by barred C and barred O.

(3) Hydrosalicylamide is warmed with HCN and a little HCl and melts to a heavy yellow oil. The aqueous layer is poured off, and the solidified oil is washed and recrystallised from boiling alcohol. The product is an orange-yellow felted mass of composition C22H16N2O3.

(4) The reaction equation is C21H18N2O3 + HCN + HCl = C22H16N2O3 + NH4Cl. Atom balance:
- Left: C 22, H 20, N 3, O 3, Cl 1.
- Right: C 22, H 20, N 3, O 3, Cl 1.
The equation balances.

(5) The product is named 'yellow hydrocyansalide'. Its properties:
- It is sparingly soluble in cold ethanol and more soluble in hot ethanol.
- It is neutral and very stable to baryta water and dilute H2SO4.
- In a sealed tube it decomposes slowly to CO2, NH3 and salicylaldehyde ('salicylige Säure').
- Several days' boiling in alcohol converts it to an isomer. The continuation on p. 388 describes this as brown needles, the 'brown hydrocyansalide'.

There is no derivation, number theory or analysis on the page.
errors: No errors found: the displayed equation is atom-balanced and the formula C21H18N2O3 for hydrosalicylamide is correct.
The motivating hope (an indigo/isatin product from adding carbon to a salicyl compound) is speculative, but this is chemistry, not a mathematical error.

results.what: Reaction of hydrosalicylamide with HCN/HCl giving C22H16N2O3 ('yellow hydrocyansalide') plus NH4Cl, and its isomerisation to a brown form
results.modern_name: Strecker-type reaction of an aromatic aldehyde hydramide (aminonitrile/cyanide addition chemistry)
results.usually_credited_to: F. Beilstein and A. Reinecke (c. 1858-59); the Strecker reaction to A. Strecker (1850)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed chemistry article by Beilstein, not Riemann's work. Its presence in the 'Primzahlen' bundle is presumably as scrap or wrapper paper. It has no mathematical content.

checkable.asserts: C21H18N2O3 + CNH + HCl = C22H16N2O3 + NH4Cl is atom-balanced (order C,H,N,O,Cl).
Hydrosalicylamide C21H18N2O3 = 3 salicylaldehyde + 2 NH3 - 3 H2O (order C,H,N,O).
The molar mass of C22H16N2O3 is about 356.4 g/mol.

transcription_corrections: The C and O in the formulas are printed as barred letters (Ꞓ, Ꝋ), the 1850s notation for the doubled atomic weights C=12, O=16. The transcription renders them as plain C and O.
The margin '13' is the archival folio number (Bl. 13), not part of the printed text.
The transcription 'zugeschmolzen Rohr' matches the print (sic, for 'zugeschmolzenen').
